description: The pie chart represents the distribution of various mathematical problem-solving skills across different educational levels, as assessed by the Odyssey Math data. There are a total of 15 slices, each corresponding to a different mathematical category. The largest slice represents Algebra at the Olympiad level, accounting for 21.19% (82 out of 382 total instances). The second-largest slice is Algebra at the High School level with 17.83% (69 out of 382 total instances). The third-largest slice is Geometry at the Olympiad level with 6.46% (25 out of 382 total instances), followed by Geometry at the High School level with 3.62% (14 out of 382 total instances). The smallest slice is Statistics at the University level with 4.39% (17 out of 382 total instances). The chart includes percentage labels inside the slices and a legend that matches the colors of the slices to their respective categories. The slices are not visually emphasized in any particular way, and the chart does not include a title or any other descriptive text.
